## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] The PD COMM authors report that the trial could not be blinded, that outcomes were questionnaires completed by participants or carers (with possible performance bias), and that recruitment closed at 388 of 546 planned participants (71% of target) after the covid-19 pandemic; the NIHR report likewise states that recruitment did not meet the pre-specified power, and Parkinson's UK commented that the findings may be less clear-cut than they first appear because NHS speech and language therapy varies widely and there is no consensus on what 'standard' therapy is. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11232530/ · keywords: LSVT BIG, LSVT LOUD and speech-language therapy · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11474952/, https://www.parkinsons.org.uk/news/2024/results-major-study-speech-and-language-therapy-parkinsons-published
- [statement] Reported effects of LSVT LOUD on speech intelligibility are mixed: RCSLT guidance (last updated December 2025) says eight studies reported improvement and two did not, depending on how intelligibility was measured; the Cochrane review comparing therapy techniques (searches up to April 2011) says all included trials assessed intelligibility and almost all results were not statistically significant; and a meta-analysis by Pu and colleagues reported pooled speech intelligibility of 16.54 (95% CI 11.35-21.72) with heterogeneity of 77%. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.rcslt.org/members/clinical-guidance/parkinsons/parkinsons-guidance/ · keywords: LSVT BIG, LSVT LOUD and speech-language therapy · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7120320/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8782619/

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] In PD COMM, a pragmatic, UK-based, unblinded, three-arm randomised trial of 388 people with Parkinson's disease and dysarthria, the primary outcome (self-reported Voice Handicap Index total score at three months, where a low score is positive) was lower with LSVT LOUD than with no speech and language therapy (-8.0 points; 99% confidence interval -13.3 to -2.6; P<0.001) and lower than with NHS speech and language therapy (-9.6 points; -14.9 to -4.4). (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11232530/ · keywords: LSVT BIG, LSVT LOUD and speech-language therapy · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11474952/
- [statement] In PD COMM, the Voice Handicap Index total score remained lower with LSVT LOUD than with no speech and language therapy at six months (-7.2; 99% confidence interval -13.3 to -1.1) and at 12 months (-6.7; -12.6 to -0.8); the authors write that re-intervention might still be required should the treatment effect wear off or as Parkinson's disease progresses. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11232530/ · keywords: LSVT BIG, LSVT LOUD and speech-language therapy · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11474952/
- [statement] In a randomized controlled trial funded by the National Institutes of Health and LSVT Global, Inc. (several authors report employment or consulting roles with LSVT Global), 64 participants with Parkinson's disease were randomized to LSVT LOUD, LSVT ARTIC or no treatment; sound pressure level (the primary outcome) improved more with LSVT LOUD than with LSVT ARTIC or no treatment at 1 and 7 months, while between-group differences in the participant-reported CETI-M were not significant at 7 months (P = 0.08). (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6261685/ · keywords: LSVT BIG, LSVT LOUD and speech-language therapy
- [statement] NICE guideline NG71, published 19 July 2017 and last reviewed 19 December 2024, recommends offering speech and language therapy to people with Parkinson's disease who are experiencing problems with communication, swallowing or saliva (recommendation 1.7.8), including strategies to improve speech and communication 'such as attention to effort therapies'; Parkinson's UK's summary of the NICE guideline and the Canadian guideline for Parkinson disease (which grades the recommendation A and cites NICE as its source) restate it. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/Recommendations · keywords: LSVT BIG, LSVT LOUD and speech-language therapy · also: https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71, https://www.parkinsons.org.uk/information/healthcare/nice-guidelines, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6733687/
- [statement] Two speech-therapy guidance documents name LSVT: the Royal College of Speech and Language Therapists' Parkinson's guidance (last updated December 2025) states that LSVT LOUD is highly recommended for communication problems in people with Parkinson's, calls it the only behavioural treatment with strong evidence for managing dysarthria (supported by 40 studies), and recommends telehealth in specific well-defined treatments such as LSVT LOUD; the Dutch guideline for speech-language therapy in Parkinson's disease (Dutch text published in 2008; English edition copyright 2011) strongly recommends PLVT or LSVT for people with hypokinetic dysarthria who satisfy the indications for intensive treatment. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.rcslt.org/members/clinical-guidance/parkinsons/parkinsons-guidance/ · keywords: LSVT BIG, LSVT LOUD and speech-language therapy · also: https://www.parkinsonnet.nl/app/uploads/sites/3/2019/11/dutch_slp_guidelines-final.pdf
- [statement] In a systematic review and meta-analysis of LSVT-BIG (searched to September 2017; three randomised trials of 84 participants with mild Parkinson's disease), UPDRS part III improved more than with physiotherapy exercises or a shorter training protocol (mean difference -3.20; 95% CI -5.18 to -1.23), whereas Timed Up and Go (-0.47; 95% CI -0.99 to 0.06) and 10-metre walk (-0.53; 95% CI -1.07 to 0.01) showed only trends, and the authors call this preliminary, moderate quality evidence; a separate gait-exercise meta-analysis (Ni and colleagues) described the LSVT program as yielding only a trend toward increased walking speed. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28980476/ · keywords: LSVT BIG, LSVT LOUD and speech-language therapy · also: https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/full/10.1177/1545968318801558

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] The PD COMM pilot trial reported a trend to improvement in the Voice Handicap Index at three months with both LSVT LOUD and standard speech and language therapy versus control, whereas the full PD COMM trial reported benefit for LSVT LOUD but no evidence of benefit for NHS speech and language therapy versus no therapy. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5763537/ · keywords: LSVT BIG, LSVT LOUD and speech-language therapy · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11232530/
- [statement] Two meta-analyses of randomized trials report greater vocal intensity (sound pressure level) after LSVT than with control interventions: one pooled 141 participants and found a higher level with LSVT of 7.36 dB (95% CI 6.60-8.12) immediately after treatment, and the other reported increases of 8.87, 4.34, 3.25 and 3.31 dB for sustained 'Ah' phonation, Rainbow passage reading, monologue and picture description after one month versus no intervention; both sets of authors state that larger randomized trials are needed. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8782619/ · keywords: LSVT BIG, LSVT LOUD and speech-language therapy · also: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32539227/
- [statement] Two Cochrane reviews with literature searches up to April 2011 each concluded that evidence was insufficient: the review of speech and language therapy versus placebo or no intervention (three randomised trials, 63 participants) found insufficient evidence to conclusively support or refute efficacy for speech problems in Parkinson's disease, and the review comparing therapy techniques (six trials, 159 patients) found insufficient evidence to support or refute any form of therapy over another; the PD COMM authors summarise the earlier review as showing insufficient evidence because of few trials, limited sample sizes and high risk of bias. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7098084/ · keywords: LSVT BIG, LSVT LOUD and speech-language therapy · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7120320/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11232530/
- [statement] In the Berlin LSVT BIG study (60 patients with mild to moderate Parkinson's disease randomly assigned to one-to-one LSVT BIG, group Nordic Walking or unsupervised domestic exercises; UPDRS scores from blinded video rating), the mean UPDRS motor improvement at 16 weeks was -5.05 (SD 3.91) with LSVT BIG versus a mild deterioration of 0.58 (SD 3.17) with Nordic Walking and 1.68 (SD 5.95) with domestic exercise, with no significant group differences in quality of life (PDQ39). (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20669294/ · keywords: LSVT BIG, LSVT LOUD and speech-language therapy · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3316992/
- [statement] Two small randomised trials of reduced-dose LSVT BIG protocols differ in what they report: a trial of a 2-week short protocol with identical exercises found motor performance equally improved versus standard LSVT BIG, whereas a trial of a modified protocol (twice weekly in clinic and twice weekly at home) reported the standard protocol favoured on some balance and gait measures. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24872078/ · keywords: LSVT BIG, LSVT LOUD and speech-language therapy · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10918598/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] A review by LSVT researchers, two of whom disclose ownership interest in LSVT Global, Inc., tabulates LSVT LOUD and LSVT BIG as standardized protocols with a dosage of 4 consecutive days a week for 4 weeks (16 sessions in one month); the PD COMM trial likewise delivered LSVT LOUD as four sessions each week over four weeks. (high confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3316992/ · keywords: LSVT BIG, LSVT LOUD and speech-language therapy · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6261685/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11232530/
- [statement] In a published comparison table of the two programmes, LSVT LOUD directs increased movement amplitude predominately to the respiratory/laryngeal systems whereas LSVT BIG directs it across the limb motor system including gait; the Berlin LSVT BIG study report describes LSVT BIG as focusing on intensive exercising of high-amplitude movements. (high confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3316992/ · keywords: LSVT BIG, LSVT LOUD and speech-language therapy · also: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20669294/
- [statement] In PD COMM, where only adverse events specific to speech and language therapy or serious events related to vocal strain or injury were reported, 93 adverse events (predominately vocal strain) were recorded in the LSVT LOUD group and 46 in the NHS speech and language therapy group, none in the no-therapy group, and no serious adverse events; the authors describe the higher rate of vocal strain with LSVT LOUD as mostly a minor, transient issue. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11232530/ · keywords: LSVT BIG, LSVT LOUD and speech-language therapy · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11474952/
- [statement] Randomised trials of remote delivery of LSVT LOUD report outcomes comparable to face-to-face delivery: Constantinescu and colleagues confirmed non-inferiority of online delivery for the primary outcome (mean change in sound pressure level on a monologue task); Theodoros and colleagues, in a single-blinded noninferiority trial (31 participants randomly assigned to face-to-face or online treatment, plus 21 non-metropolitan participants treated online), confirmed noninferiority of online treatment; and a 2025 pilot trial of 20 people comparing teletherapy with face-to-face LSVT LOUD concluded that both appear effective and that larger studies are needed. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21281410/ · keywords: LSVT BIG, LSVT LOUD and speech-language therapy · also: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27145396/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12034115/

## Research summary — LSVT BIG, LSVT LOUD and speech-language therapy

LSVT LOUD and LSVT BIG are standardized, intensive programmes (16 sessions over four weeks) that train the amplitude of voice or limb movement. In the PD COMM trial of 388 people, LSVT LOUD lowered self-reported voice handicap versus no therapy and versus NHS speech and language therapy, with benefit still present at 12 months and mostly minor vocal-strain adverse events. Two Cochrane reviews (searches to April 2011) found insufficient evidence; later meta-analyses report higher vocal loudness, while intelligibility results are mixed. NICE NG71 recommends speech and language therapy including attention to effort therapies; RCSLT guidance (December 2025) highly recommends LSVT LOUD. For LSVT BIG, the Berlin trial reported UPDRS motor gains, but a meta-analysis found only trends for walking and rated evidence preliminary.

## Source disagreement — LSVT BIG, LSVT LOUD and speech-language therapy

Session length for LSVT LOUD differs by source: Ramig and colleagues describe 16 individual 1-hour sessions in 1 month, whereas PD COMM and the Dutch guideline describe 50-minute sessions four times a week for four weeks.

## Source disagreement — LSVT BIG, LSVT LOUD and speech-language therapy

The Constantinescu abstract reports non-significant main effects for the LSVT environment, dysarthria severity and interaction effects for all outcome measures, whereas the Cochrane review states that sustained phonation loudness did not support the equivalence of online and face-to-face delivery and was significant in favour of face-to-face delivery.

Gate verdict: `SUPPORTED`. Auxiliary assertion: `prose:5fbc9a0f6fe06fe5a11af0a84caa02569b5f510d0d2e93343e89c7f88399980a`. Statement hash: `5fbc9a0f6fe06fe5a11af0a84caa02569b5f510d0d2e93343e89c7f88399980a`.

Evidence IDs: `ev:857952f70e79b5921456d34e052749292217bf973d89eff0a4cd78f15cc057ce`, `ev:a6282840b8708a10a4c8a9be4d9dfc0bf6402dcfb46c42ffe27ffab3394488c7`.

Sources: [source 1](<https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7120320/>) · [source 2](<https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21281410/>)

## Source disagreement — LSVT BIG, LSVT LOUD and speech-language therapy

NICE NG71 recommendation 1.7.8 gives attention to effort therapies as its example of speech and communication strategies, whereas RCSLT guidance (December 2025) states that LSVT LOUD is the only behavioural treatment with strong evidence for managing dysarthria.

Gate verdict: `SUPPORTED`. Auxiliary assertion: `prose:f4219a9e69b975cb2084a1d12905dec790efb7276c8a4f4f5186fe58ae7789ab`. Statement hash: `f4219a9e69b975cb2084a1d12905dec790efb7276c8a4f4f5186fe58ae7789ab`.

## Source disagreement — LSVT BIG, LSVT LOUD and speech-language therapy

Parkinson's UK says questionnaires were completed at 3, 6 and 9 months, whereas the BMJ trial report says follow-up was at three, six, and 12 months after randomisation.
